nh_wm_north_conway.blurb: North Conway sits in New Hampshire's Mount Washington Valley, and the climbing around it is on solid granite cliffs. Humphrey's Ledge, the largest sub-area, lies just west of town and feels calmer than its better-known neighbours. Trad is the main roped style, with a smaller helping of sport and a large bouldering contingent. Roped grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.10, and boulder problems range from VB up to V8. Winter adds ice, mostly WI3 and WI4, plus a few mixed lines in the M6 to M8 range. The ice season often stretches from December into March. Saco Crag and The Pig Pen are smaller crags nearby.

qc_les_dames.blurb: Les Dames is a boulder-focused zone in Val-David, in Quebec's Laurentians, and the first stop inside the regional park there. It splits into six sectors; Elizabeth and Louise hold the most problems, followed by Francoise and Martine. Bouldering dominates, with a smaller number of trad lines and a handful of sport routes. Problems start at V0 and climb all the way to V13, with plenty of easy and mid-grade options and a decent number from V6 upward. From the trailhead you walk uphill over low-angle slabs, then turn into the woods, and the main boulders begin a short way in. Val-David has been a popular bouldering centre since the 1980s.

ut_new_joe_s.blurb: New Joe's is the bouldering zone of Joe's Valley in central Utah, set on a hillside and canyon a few miles from the Left and Right Forks. Everything here is bouldering on sandstone, a porous rock that loses strength when damp. Area 51 is the most visited sector and the easiest to reach, with more boulders a short walk beyond it. The Wash Boulders hold the most problems, followed by Area 51, The Closet and Anarchy. Grades run from VB to V13, but the bulk sit between V1 and V4, with a steady supply through V8 for stronger climbers. The valley sits near 7,000 feet, so afternoons run hot, nights turn chilly, and winters are snowy.

va_bluefield_boulders.blurb: Bluefield Boulders is a small sandstone boulder field on East River Mountain, right on the Virginia and West Virginia line in Southwest Virginia. It is all bouldering: short steep walls, roofs and aretes, with a mix of crimps and good slopers. Most problems are on the shorter side and tend to be powerful. Grades run from V0 to V8, with the bulk between V3 and V6, so it suits climbers working mid-range difficulty. The walk in is almost nothing. The Main Boulder Area is the core of the climbing, and a few more boulders sit along the road.

bc_kamloops.blurb: Kamloops, in southern British Columbia, offers a scatter of smaller crags rather than one big cliff, mostly an hour or so from town. Sport leads, backed by a good amount of trad and bouldering and a few top-rope lines. Roped grades run from 5.7 to 5.13, concentrated around 5.10 and 5.11, with boulder problems up to V9. Roche Lake is the heart of the sport climbing and holds the steeper, harder routes. The Beach is the gentlest and suits newer sport climbers. The Hen House is granite, with slabs and vertical faces and a mix of trad and sport. Oregon Jack also draws ice climbers in winter. The rock season runs roughly March to November, and high summer can be hot.

ca_holcomb_valley_bouldering.blurb: Holcomb Valley Bouldering is a forest-scattered boulder zone in the San Bernardino Mountains near Big Bear Lake, at roughly 7,500 feet. Nearly everything is bouldering on granite that varies from grainy and blank to well featured and weathered. East Side Bouldering holds most of the problems, mostly moderate with flat landings, and Southside Bouldering and the North Parking Lot Boulders add more. Grades skew friendly: lots of VB through V3, tapering to a few V5s, which makes it a good place for newer boulderers and mid-grade sessions. Established problems cluster around the north and south parking areas, with room for new lines further north.
